candidates.change_summary: Change the returned selector from ERC721TokenReceiver.onERC721Received.selector to a hardcoded different selector value (0x150b7a02).
Return the zero selector (bytes4(0)) instead of the expected selector.
Return the selector computed from keccak256 of a different function signature, causing a different bytes4 return value.
Set baseToken to address(0) unconditionally instead of assigning the provided _baseToken parameter.
Assign baseToken to msg.sender instead of the provided _baseToken parameter.
Delay assignment of baseToken until after setting initialized (swap order), so baseToken remains default if initialized check manipulated externally.
Assign baseToken to address(factory) instead of the provided _baseToken parameter.
Assigns nft after setting other fields instead of before (moves nft assignment to after initialized=true), changing nft if initialize reverts or other logic interacts with nft earlier.
Sets nft to address(0) instead of provided _nft, causing nft to differ after initialize.
Deletes the assignment to nft, so nft remains its previous value after initialize.
Replace the assignment to changeFee with assigning zero (changeFee = 0), so initialize always sets changeFee to 0 regardless of input.
Replace the assignment to changeFee with assigning the provided fee parameter multiplied by 2 (changeFee = _changeFee * 2), doubling the stored changeFee.
Replace the assignment to changeFee with assigning the provided fee parameter plus 1 (changeFee = _changeFee + 1), incrementing the stored changeFee by one.
Change the assignment to feeRate to instead assign a capped value (min of provided _feeRate and 1000), altering stored feeRate after initialize.
Change the feeRate limit check from > 5000 to >= 5000 so initialize rejects feeRate == 5000 (prevents initialized from being set for that input).
Remove the final assignment that sets initialized = true by replacing it with a no-op comment so initialize leaves initialized false.
Move the initialized = true assignment to occur before setting other state so initialized becomes true even if later assignments revert (observable change).
